Best AI Video Generators in 2026 for Creating 1-Minute Videos

Want to create a one-minute video without filming everything yourself? Explore AI video generators that can turn text prompts and images into video clips, plus learn how to combine those clips into a complete 60-second video for YouTube Shorts, TikTok, and other platforms.

By LokkeeVerse · 13 min read

Introduction

Creating a one-minute video no longer requires a camera, expensive equipment, or advanced video editing skills. AI video generators can transform written prompts and images into moving scenes that you can use for social media content, product advertisements, storytelling, and educational videos.

However, choosing the right AI video generator can be confusing. Some tools focus on realistic scenes, while others offer creative effects, advanced editing features, or workflows that help you produce multiple clips for a longer video.

If your goal is to create a complete 60-second video, there is one important thing to understand: generating a one-minute video in a single step is different from creating several shorter clips and combining them. Many AI video workflows use the second approach because it gives creators more control over each scene.

In this guide, we explore five AI video generators worth considering in 2026, what each one can help you create, and how to turn their output into a complete one-minute video.

Can Runway create a one-minute video?

How to Create a 60-Second Video With AI

You do not always need one AI tool to do everything. A practical workflow combines AI-generated scenes with a video editor, narration, captions, and music.

Here is a simple method you can follow.

Step 1: Choose a video idea

Start with one clear topic. For example:

  • A 60-second motivational video.
  • A short story with a surprising ending.
  • A product advertisement for an online store.
  • An educational video explaining an interesting fact.
  • A faceless YouTube Short about technology.

A focused idea makes it easier to keep your video interesting from beginning to end.

Step 2: Write a short script

Divide your script into an opening, main content, and conclusion.

For a 60-second video, you could plan:

  • 0–5 seconds: An attention-grabbing opening.
  • 5–20 seconds: Introduce the topic.
  • 20–45 seconds: Show the main scenes or explain the idea.
  • 45–55 seconds: Deliver the key message or reveal.
  • 55–60 seconds: End with a call to action or memorable final shot.

These are planning guidelines rather than fixed rules. Adjust them to suit your content.

Step 3: Turn the script into scenes

Break the script into several visual scenes. For example, a product advertisement might contain an opening shot, a product close-up, a demonstration, and a final promotional scene.

Write a separate prompt for each scene. Describe the subject, location, camera movement, lighting, and desired visual style.

Step 4: Generate the clips

Choose an AI video generator based on the visual style and workflow you need.

Generate the scenes individually and review the results. If a clip contains distorted objects, inconsistent characters, or unwanted movement, adjust the prompt and try again if your credits allow it.

Remember that AI generation is not guaranteed to produce the exact result you describe.

Step 5: Combine the clips

Import the clips into a video editor and arrange them in the correct order.

Trim unnecessary moments, add transitions where appropriate, and make sure the scenes flow naturally. You can also add narration, subtitles, sound effects, and background music.

Step 6: Export and review

For TikTok and YouTube Shorts, a vertical 9:16 format is usually a practical choice.

Check that the finished video is approximately 60 seconds, the text is readable on a phone, the audio is clear, and the opening captures attention quickly.

Before publishing, confirm that the tools and assets you used permit your intended use.

A Useful AI Video Prompt for One-Minute Content

You can adapt this prompt for a short AI-generated video project:

"Create a cinematic vertical video for social media about a young entrepreneur building a small online business. Show the entrepreneur working on a laptop, planning content, reviewing product images, and celebrating a completed project. Use realistic lighting, smooth camera movement, natural-looking environments, and a consistent visual style. Compose the footage for a 9:16 vertical video. Avoid distorted hands, unreadable text, and sudden changes in the main character's appearance."

This prompt describes the overall concept. For more control, split it into separate scene prompts and generate each scene individually.

Do not expect a single generation to produce a complete, perfectly edited 60-second video. The result depends on the tool and the settings you use.

What Should You Consider Before Choosing an AI Video Generator?

The best platform for you depends on more than visual quality.

Video duration

Check the maximum duration supported by the specific model you plan to use. A tool that generates excellent short clips may still require extra editing to produce a full minute.

Generation credits

AI video generation can consume credits quickly, particularly when you need several scenes or repeated attempts. Check how many generations your plan supports.

Visual quality

Look for consistent subjects, natural movement, convincing backgrounds, and fewer visual errors. Test the tool with a prompt similar to the video you actually want to make.

Editing features

If you plan to create complete videos regularly, consider whether you need a separate editor for trimming clips, adding subtitles, balancing audio, and exporting the finished video.

Watermarks and commercial use

A tool may let you experiment for free but restrict exports, credits, or commercial use. Review the latest terms before using generated footage in client projects or monetized content.

Ease of use

Beginners may prefer a simple interface and straightforward workflow. Experienced creators may prioritize greater control over scenes, motion, and post-production.

Which AI Video Generator Should You Choose?

There is no single winner for every creator. Your best option depends on the type of video you want to make.

  • Choose Runway to explore AI generation alongside creative production tools.
  • Explore Google Veo if you want to create cinematic scenes using Google's video models.
  • Try Kling AI if image animation and prompt-based video generation suit your project.
  • Consider Pika for creative effects and experimental short videos.
  • Compare Luma if you want another option for developing AI-generated footage.

These are use-case suggestions, not results from a completed head-to-head test. Features, prices, and access can change, so verify the latest information on each official website before choosing a subscription.

Final Thoughts

AI video generators can make it easier to create a one-minute video for YouTube Shorts, TikTok, marketing campaigns, and other projects. They can help you develop visual scenes without recording every shot yourself.

However, the most practical workflow often involves more than pressing one button. You may need to write a script, generate multiple clips, select the best results, add audio, and edit everything into a coherent 60-second video.

Start with a simple project, test the available free options carefully, and choose a tool based on your desired visual style, clip duration, budget, and editing needs.

The goal is not just to generate AI footage. It is to turn that footage into a complete video that people actually want to watch.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can AI generate a full one-minute video from a single prompt?

Some AI video workflows may support longer outputs, but capabilities vary by model and interface. Many creators generate multiple shorter clips and combine them to reach 60 seconds.

What is the best AI video generator for YouTube Shorts?

Runway, Google Veo, Kling AI, Pika, and Luma are options to compare. Consider vertical video support, scene quality, clip duration, cost, and how easily you can edit the results.

Can I make one-minute AI videos for free?

You may be able to create some footage at no cost through free plans, trials, or promotional credits. However, limits can apply to credits, duration, resolution, watermarks, and commercial use.

Do I need video editing skills to create AI videos?

Not necessarily. Beginner-friendly editors can help you combine clips, add captions, and arrange scenes without advanced editing knowledge. You will still need to review the output and make adjustments when necessary.

Can I monetize videos made with AI?

Potentially, yes. Monetization depends on the platform's rules, the originality and quality of your content, and the usage rights attached to the AI tools and other assets you use. Check the applicable policies before publishing.
